topic_tag: average pay per hour worked at a bakery with a weekend premium for managers
prompt: Last week a bakery had 5 full-time bakers who each worked 40 hours at $23.60 per hour, 9 part-time clerks who each worked 16 hours at $18.40 per hour, and 3 shift managers who each worked 44 hours at a regular rate of $29.20 per hour. Of each manager's 44 hours, 10 were weekend hours, which are paid at 25% more than the manager's regular rate. No other employee worked weekend hours. For all the hours these 17 employees worked last week, what was the average pay per hour worked, to the nearest cent?
explanation: The bakers earned 5(40)(23.60) = $4,720.00 and the clerks earned 9(16)(18.40) = $2,649.60. Each manager earned 44(29.20) + 10(0.25)(29.20) = 1,284.80 + 73.00 = $1,357.80, so the managers earned $4,073.40. The total pay was $11,443.00 for 200 + 144 + 132 = 476 hours, so the average pay per hour worked is 11,443/476 = about $24.04. The option 23.58 leaves out the weekend premium. The option 23.73 averages the three hourly rates without weighting them by hours. The option 21.84 weights the three rates by the number of employees instead of by the hours worked.

topic_tag: heat loss through a wall's insulated section, windows and door, with layered R-values and air leakage
subskill: applied area: heat loss through a wall
prompt: Heat escapes through each part of a house wall at a rate, in BTU per hour, equal to the part's area in square feet times the inside-minus-outside temperature difference in °F, divided by the part's R-value. One wall has three parts: 156 square feet of insulated section, 28 square feet of windows, and a 20-square-foot door. The insulated section is built in layers whose R-values add: insulation with R-value 13, drywall with R-value 0.45, and siding with R-value 0.8. The windows have R-value 2.1, and the door has R-value 5.3. In addition, air leaking around the windows and the door carries away heat at a rate equal to 15% of the rate at which heat escapes through the windows and door themselves. When it is 70°F inside and 23°F outside, what is the total rate, to the nearest BTU per hour, at which heat escapes through this wall, including the air leakage?
explanation: The temperature difference is 70 - 23 = 47°F. The insulated section's R-value is 13 + 0.45 + 0.8 = 14.25, so it loses 156(47)/14.25 = 514.5 BTU/h. The windows lose 28(47)/2.1 = 626.7 and the door 20(47)/5.3 = 177.4, together 804.0 BTU/h, and leakage adds 15% of that, 120.6. Total: 514.5 + 804.0 + 120.6 = 1,439 BTU per hour. The option 1489 uses only the insulation's R-value 13 for the insulated section, leaving out the drywall and siding layers. The option 1516 takes 15% of the heat lost through all three parts instead of the windows and door only. The option 1449 divides the whole 204 square feet by the plain average of the three R-values, (14.25 + 2.1 + 5.3)/3, before adding the leakage.
quantity_asked: Total heat-loss rate in BTU/h: 47(156/14.25 + 1.15(28/2.1 + 20/5.3)), to the nearest whole number.

distractor_kind.1516: error path: leakage taken as 15% of all conduction, not of windows and door only. (a) no parameter extreme. (b) neighbouring base of the percent; strictly inside. (c) above the 1,319 bound; no upper bound reaches it. (d) real error: wrong base for the 15%.

rate >= whole wall at R-14.25, 204(47)/14.25 = 673: kills nothing

parts of a wall in parallel

topic_tag: evacuation time varying directly as occupancy and inversely as usable doorway width
prompt: Fire-safety planners for a concert hall use a model in which the time needed for everyone to leave the hall varies directly as the number of people in the hall and inversely as the total usable width of the open doorways. The usable width of a doorway is its actual width minus 15 centimeters on each side, because people do not walk right next to the door frame. In a drill with 640 people and 4 open doorways, each 1.1 meters wide, everyone left in 150 seconds. For a concert, 860 people will be in the hall, 1 of those 4 doorways will be closed, and 2 temporary doorways, each 0.8 meter wide, will be opened. According to the model, how many seconds will it take everyone to leave during the concert, to the nearest tenth of a second?

At the concert, 3 of the 1.1-meter doorways and the 2 temporary doorways are open, so the usable width is 3(0.8) + 2(0.8 - 0.3) = 2.4 + 1.0 = 3.4 meters. Time varies directly as people and inversely as usable width, so t = 150(860/640)(3.2/3.4) = 189.7 seconds, to the nearest tenth. The option 184.6 subtracts 15 centimeters once per doorway instead of on each side. The option 161.3 uses the number of doorways (4, then 5) in place of their widths. The option 153.6 leaves the closed doorway open (usable width 4.2 meters).

topic_tag: propane for one night when tank life varies inversely as the inside-outside temperature difference
subskill: inverse variation with a temperature difference
prompt: A greenhouse heater burns propane from a 100-gallon tank. The number of hours a full tank lasts varies inversely as the difference between the thermostat setting and the outside temperature. With the thermostat set at 65°F and a steady outside temperature of 41°F, a full tank lasts 90 hours. On a night when the outside temperature will stay at 28°F, the thermostat is lowered to 60°F. To the nearest hundredth of a gallon, how many gallons of propane will the heater burn during the 14-hour night?
explanation: The temperature difference changes from 65 - 41 = 24 degrees to 60 - 28 = 32 degrees. Tank life varies inversely as the difference, so a full tank now lasts 90(24/32) = 67.5 hours, and the heater burns 100/67.5 gallon per hour. In 14 hours it burns 14(100/67.5) = 20.74 gallons. The option 22.78 scales by the outside temperatures, 90(28/41) hours, instead of by the differences. The option 22.14 ignores the thermostat change in the difference (37 degrees) and then scales by the thermostat settings, 60/65. At a depth of 12 meters, this diver uses 48 liters of air per minute. The diver's tank holds 2,700 liters of air, and the diver must begin to surface with at least 500 liters left. The option 21.26 subtracts 6 minutes from the 27-meter time instead of subtracting the air used in those 6 minutes.

topic_tag: trip fuel when the air-resistance share of fuel use varies as the square of speed
